chats.answer:
Whole-home battery backup with generator

A whole-home battery backup system combined with a standby generator is one of the most reliable ways to keep your house powered during an outage.

The idea is to use the battery for instant, quiet backup power and the generator for extended outages. You can also integrate solar panels to reduce electricity costs and recharge the battery.

How the system works
Conceptual architecture. Actual wiring, transfer switching, and generator compatibility depend on the equipment selected.

During a power outage:

Battery takes over: Your home continues receiving electricity, often with little or no noticeable interruption.

Generator starts when needed: When battery charge gets low, a compatible controller starts the generator.

Generator powers the home and may recharge the battery: This requires a system specifically designed to support generator charging.

Battery resumes operation: The generator can shut down when sufficient charge is restored.

Grid returns: The system transfers back to normal operation.

Not every battery system supports this entire sequence automatically.

A system worth considering

FranklinWH aPower 2 + standby generator

This is a strong candidate because FranklinWH explicitly supports generator integration, automatic generator start/stop, and battery charging from the generator.

chats.answer:
Whole-home battery backup with generator

A whole-home battery backup system combined with a standby generator is one of the most reliable ways to keep your house powered during outages.

The idea is to use the battery for instant, quiet backup power and the generator for extended outages when the battery runs low.

How the system works
Conceptual architecture. Actual wiring, transfer switching, and generator compatibility depend on the equipment.

During normal operation, the grid powers the home and the battery stays charged. When the grid fails, the battery takes over almost instantly. If the outage lasts long enough, a compatible generator starts and can supply the home and recharge the battery, depending on the system design.

The important detail is that not every home battery can be charged directly by a generator. You need compatible controls, switching equipment, and an approved integration.

Systems worth considering

A strong option for a permanently installed, automatic backup system. Supported PWRcell configurations can integrate a Generac generator that also charges the battery.
